boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Chattanooga record (August 21, 1863) in the Chickamauga Campaign [August-September 1863]. NPS says the shelling continued periodically for two weeks; later shelling and Bragg's September evacuation are outside the frozen one-day interval. Campaign-wide movements, the Chattanooga evacuation and army-wide figures are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads Wilder's Brigade [US] and Hill's Corps [CS] without counts; the live field reads zero. NPS names the 18th Indiana Light Artillery as the battery ordered to shell the town. Cist says Wilder was supported by Wagner's brigade and that both commands opened fire. Hill says his corps consisted of Cleburne's and Stewart's divisions, encamped about Tyner's Station.
claims.rationale: Unit names only; no count is inspected. Live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.value: NPS says Wilder reached the Tennessee River opposite Chattanooga; Cist says the shelling was from across the river. Hill says that after the shelling he had every ford and ferry from the mouth of the Chickamauga to the mouth of the Hiwassee guarded and covered by rifle-pits and batteries.
claims.rationale: The river separated the forces; Hill's works followed the shelling and are not tagged inherited. No map verification.

claims.value: Hill says the Federals began shelling during fast-day services without notice, that pickets and scouts, if any were out, had given no warning, and that a few nights before General Clayton, sent up the river, had found no cavalry pickets for 40 miles. Cist calls it the surprise at Chattanooga. NPS says the shells caught many soldiers and civilians in church observing a day of prayer and fasting.
claims.rationale: Attributed knowledge from the Confederate corps commander, an interested history and a summary; Hill's OCR leaves the day blank ('fast day (August)').

claims.value: NPS says the brigade marched where the Confederates could see it, reinforcing Bragg's expectation of an attack from the northeast, and that the shelling helped keep his attention there. Cist says the feint under Crittenden made Bragg concentrate at and above Chattanooga. Hill says the Federal design had been to interpose a column between Knoxville and Chattanooga and isolate Buckner.
claims.rationale: Stated purposes and an opponent's inference of intent; campaign context, not a causal estimate.

open_questions: Wilder's and Wagner's reports and the Confederate garrison returns remain deferred; whether the frozen one-day record includes later shelling is not established.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Cist is an interested Union staff history. The Hill, Hindman and Bragg reports, printed in Official Records Series I, Volume XXX, Part 2, are separate families of interested Confederate commanders' accounts; the volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
